ForestGEO Panama — Tree Height Allometry, Small Plots 2011–2020

plant_scaling_data project

2026-05-01

1 Overview

ForestGEO Panama small-plots allometry is a dataset of individual tree height and diameter measurements collected across 24 small (mostly 1-ha) forest plots in central Panama between 2011 and 2020. It was compiled as part of the Smithsonian ForestGEO network to support allometric model development for tropical forests.

Ramos P, Villareal P, Muller-Landau HC (2024). Tree height allometry data for 5,109 trees in twenty-four small ForestGEO plots in Panama, 2011–2020. Smithsonian Figshare. doi: 10.25573/data.24954204.v1 License: CC BY 4.0

⚠ Citation note: The DOI and author list above are taken directly from the Figshare landing page and should be verified against the source before use in any manuscript.

3 Data dictionary

kable(dd, caption = "Variable definitions (from source xlsx data dictionary)")
Variable definitions (from source xlsx data dictionary)
Attribute name Attribute Label Category Character type Units Definition
UniqueID Unique tree ID Anything String NA Combination of plotname and tag that is unique for each tree (the same tag number may appear in different plots)
PX_m X cartesian coordinates Numeric Non-integer Meters Location of the tree within the plot along a cartesian X axis (in m)
PY_m Y cartesian coordinates Numeric Non-integer Meters Location of the tree within the plot along a cartesian Y axis (in m)
Plotname Plot name Unordered category String NA Code for the plot in which the tree is located
Tag Tree tag Numeric Integer NA Tag number of the tree
Stem Stem number Ordered category Integer NA Stem number - blank if there is only one stem ever
MultiStem Multiple-stemmed Unordered category Boolean NA True/false - Are there multiple stems of this tree in this dataset?
sp6 6 letter species code Anything String NA 6-letter code for species ID
LatinBinomial Latin binomial Anything String NA Tree species latin binomial
HOM_m Height of meassurement Numeric Non-integer Meters Height of measurement (in m); height along stem at which the diameter was measured (marked with paint)
DBH_mm Diameter at breast height Numeric Non-integer Milimeters Diameter of the stem (in mm) at the paint-marked point
Crown Crown Ordered category Integer NA Crown intactness score. values 0 to 4. 4 = 75-100% of the crown is intact (no or few branches lost) 3 = 50-75% of the crown is intact 2 = 25-50% of the crown is intact 1 = 0-25% of the crown is intact (most of the crown is gone)
Light Light Ordered category Integer NA Crown illumination index. values 1 to 5. 5 = crown completely exposed (to vertical light and to lateral light within the 90 degree inverted cone encompassing the crown) 4 = full overhead light (>=90% of the vertical projection of the crown exposed to vertical light; later light blocked within some or all of the 90 degree inverted cone encompassing the crown) 3 = some overhead light (10-90% of the vertical project of the crown exposed to vertical light) 2 = lateral light (<10% of the vertical project of the crown exposed to vertical light; crown lit laterally) 1 = no direct light (crown not lit directly either vertically or laterally)
Lianas Lianas Ordered category Integer NA Liana cover of the crown. values 0 to 4. where 0 is no lianas. 1 is 1-25% covered with lianas. 2 is 26-50%. 3 is 51-75%. and 4 is 76-100%
Q Quebrado Unordered category Boolean NA True/false - Stem broken above 1.3 m
TreeHt_m Tree Height Numeric Non-integer Meters Tree height (m)
Observer Observer Anything String NA Who made the measurements?
DD Day Numeric Integer NA Day of the month in which the measurement was taken
MM Month Numeric Integer NA Month of the year in which the measurement was taken
YYYY Year Numeric Integer NA Year in which the measurement was taken
L Leaning Unordered category Boolean NA True/false - Is the tree leaning by more than 45 degrees?
PP Placa Perdida Unordered category Boolean NA True/false - Was the tree tag missing when on the measurement date?
R Resprout Unordered category Boolean NA True/false - Is the stem a resprout? (Was it broken below 1.3 m)
Notes Notes Anything String NA Any additional notes made by the field team (mostly in Spanish)

Note: Column B appears in the data file (25 columns total) but has no entry in the 24-row data dictionary. All 5,109 values are FALSE. It may represent a broken-below-breast-height flag analogous to Q (broken above 1.3 m); the exact definition is undocumented in the deposited files.

4 Geographic context

# No global lat/lon in the dataset — plots use local Cartesian coordinates.
# We show the approximate study region in Panama.
world <- map_data("world")

panama_pt <- data.frame(
  label = "24 ForestGEO small plots\n(central Panama)",
  lon   = -79.8,
  lat   =   9.1
)

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = world,
               aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
               fill = "grey88", color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = panama_pt,
             aes(x = lon, y = lat),
             color = "#e41a1c", size = 5) +
  geom_text(data = panama_pt,
            aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = label),
            hjust = -0.08, vjust = 0.5, size = 3.5, color = "#e41a1c") +
  coord_fixed(1.3, xlim = c(-120, -30), ylim = c(-15, 35)) +
  labs(
    title    = "ForestGEO Panama small plots \u2014 approximate study region",
    subtitle = paste0("\u26a0 No lat/lon in source file. ",
                      "Exact plot coordinates are in the ForestGEO site registry ",
                      "(https://forestgeo.si.edu/sites)."),
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank())

5 Per-plot tree counts

plot_counts <- dat |>

ggplot(plot_counts, aes(x = reorder(Plotname, n_trees), y = n_trees,
                        fill = n_trees)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n_trees), hjust = -0.1, size = 3.2) +

  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "N trees", title = "Trees per plot (24 plots)")

    title = "DBH distribution \u2014 ForestGEO Panama (n = 5,109)",

8 Height ~ DBH scaling

sub <- dat |> filter(!is.na(TreeHt_m), DBH_cm > 0, TreeHt_m > 0)
lm_fit <- lm(log(TreeHt_m) ~ log(DBH_cm), data = sub)
beta <- round(coef(lm_fit)[2], 3)
r2   <- round(summary(lm_fit)$r.squared, 3)

sub |>
  ggplot(aes(x = DBH_cm, y = TreeHt_m)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.7, color = "#2ca25f") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", linewidth = 1.2, se = TRUE) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma) + scale_y_log10(labels = comma) +
  annotation_logticks() +
  labs(
    x = "DBH (cm)", y = "Height (m)",
    title = "Height \u223c DBH  (OLS log-log regression)",
    subtitle = paste0("\u03b2 = ", beta, "   R\u00b2 = ", r2,
                      "   n = ", nrow(sub))
  )

OLS log-log regression on all individuals with valid DBH and height. \(\beta \approx 0.6\)–\(0.7\) is typical for tropical moist forest. ⚠ This regression pools all plots and species and should not be treated as a formal allometric model — use SMA regression and species-level grouping for inference.

9 Height of measurement (HOM)

pct_standard <- round(100 * mean(dat$HOM_m == 1.3), 1)

dat |>
  ggplot(aes(x = HOM_m)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1, fill = "#d6604d", color = "white",
                 linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1.3, linetype = "dashed", color = "black",
             linewidth = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = 1.42, y = Inf, label = "Standard 1.3 m BH",
           hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(
    x = "HOM (m)", y = "N trees",
    title = "Height of measurement (HOM) distribution",
    subtitle = paste0(pct_standard, "% at standard 1.3 m; remainder elevated above buttresses")
  )

Key caveat: Diameter is measured at a paint-marked point (HOM_m) ranging from 0.3 to 4.8 m. Trees with HOM_m > 1.3 are typically buttressed individuals measured above the buttress. This must be accounted for in any allometric comparison that assumes DBH at breast height (1.3 m).

10 Quality and condition flags

flags <- data.frame(
  Flag = c(
    "Q — stem broken above 1.3 m (Quebrado)",
    "L — leaning > 45\u00b0",
    "PP — tag missing at measurement date (Placa Perdida)",
    "R — resprout (stem broken below 1.3 m)",
    "B — undocumented flag (all FALSE; not in data dictionary)",
    "MultiStem — tree has multiple stems in dataset"
  ),
  N_TRUE = c(
    sum(dat$Q,         na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(dat$L,         na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(dat$PP,        na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(dat$R,         na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(dat$B,         na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(dat$MultiStem, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  Pct = paste0(round(100 * c(
    mean(dat$Q,         na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(dat$L,         na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(dat$PP,        na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(dat$R,         na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(dat$B,         na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(dat$MultiStem, na.rm = TRUE)
  ), 1), "%"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

16 Data completeness

key_cols <- c("DBH_mm", "TreeHt_m", "HOM_m", "LatinBinomial",
              "Plotname", "Crown", "Light", "Lianas", "YYYY", "Observer")

compl_df <- data.frame(
  Column       = key_cols,
  N_nonNA      = sapply(key_cols, function(c) sum(!is.na(dat[[c]]))),
  Pct_complete = paste0(
    sapply(key_cols, function(c) round(100 * mean(!is.na(dat[[c]])), 1)),
    "%"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE

17 Notes for allometric merging

  1. DBH units: Raw data are in mm — convert to cm (DBH_cm = DBH_mm / 10) before merging with BAAD, Tallo, Niklas-Enquist, or NEON (all use cm or the equivalent SI unit).

  2. Non-standard HOM: Diameter is measured at a paint-marked point varying from 0.3 to 4.8 m. Trees with HOM_m > 1.3 m are buttressed individuals. Allometries that assume DBH at 1.3 m BH should flag these or apply a buttress correction (e.g., Cushman et al. 2014, For. Ecol. Manage.).

  3. No global lat/lon: The dataset uses plot-local Cartesian coordinates (PX_m, PY_m). Global coordinates must be retrieved from the ForestGEO site registry (https://forestgeo.si.edu/sites) before any spatial analysis or merging with georeferenced datasets.

  4. No AGB in source: Only diameters and heights are provided. AGB must be estimated by applying an allometric equation (e.g., Chave et al. 2014 pantropical equation), which requires a wood density lookup (Zanne et al. 2009 backbone via BIOMASS R package).

  5. Taxonomy: Species are identified to LatinBinomial with no authority or taxonomic backbone. TNRS or GBIF name matching is recommended before any cross-source taxonomic merge.

  6. Undocumented B column: All 5,109 values are FALSE. No definition appears in the deposited data dictionary; confirm with data depositors if this flag is relevant before excluding or retaining records.
